title: Additive induction on a finite rational root pairing with a base
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $M,N$ be vector spaces over the field $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], let $P:\mathrm{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ M\ N$ be a crystallographic root pairing in the Mathlib sense, and let $b:P.\mathrm{Base}$. Thus $P$ has injective root and coroot families and a bilinear pairing with the usual simultaneous reflection permutations and root-coroot value $2$; crystallographic means that root-coroot values are integers. The base $b$ has finite support $D\subseteq I$, linearly independent root and coroot families on $D$, and each root and each coroot or its negative is a nonnegative integral sum from its respective family on $D$. Write $a_i=P.\mathrm{root}(i)$ and $-i=P.\mathrm{reflectionPerm}(i)(i)$, so $a_{-i}=-a_i$. For any predicate $Q:I\to\mathrm{Prop}$, if (i) $Q(i)\Rightarrow Q(-i)$ for every $i$, (ii) $Q(j)$ for every $j\in D$, and (iii) $Q(i)$ and $j\in D$ and $a_k=a_i+a_j$ imply $Q(k)$, then $Q(i)$ for all $i\in I$.
